platform.database: One primary Aurora PostgreSQL cluster with PostGIS (one database). Each service owns one schema and is the only writer of its tables; every other service gets read-only access through the shared zudomart_readers role, granted per table/column in the owner's migrations. One login role per service (svc_<service>).

ownership.go: accounts/users, wallet/ledger, payments, marketplace (catalog, inventory), orders
ownership.typescript: social orchestration (posts, feed, notifications, media metadata)

platform.events: RabbitMQ adopted (owner, 2026-10-03). No Kafka on day one. Business write + outbox row commit in one Postgres transaction; a relay publishes through the DomainEventPublisher interface with publisher confirms and mandatory routing to the durable RabbitMQ topic exchange zudomart.events (routing key = event name <entity>.<pastTense>, message_id = event id, envelope.v1 unchanged). Each consumer service owns one durable quorum queue bound to the routing keys it needs (replaces the SNS to SQS fan-out and filter policies); unrouted events go to the alternate exchange zudomart.unrouted. Locally RabbitMQ 4 in Docker; in AWS Amazon MQ for RabbitMQ, cluster deployment (3 brokers across AZs) in private subnets, TLS, one least-privilege user per service. The SNS/SQS adapters stay behind EVENT_BUS=sqs until the cut-over is proven.
platform.jobs: Background jobs (email incl. throttled bulk batches and digests, media processing, reports, ad reports, payouts, search indexing, trust advisories) go through the JobQueue interface: direct exchange zudomart.jobs with one quorum queue per job type (routing key = queue name). Retries use per-queue delay queues <queue>.retry.30s/2m/10m/30m (TTL + dead-letter back to the queue, no plugins), then <queue>.dlq after 5 attempts; poison messages go straight to the DLQ. Consumers use manual acks, prefetch limits and are idempotent on the job/event id. Delayed jobs use the largest retry tier that fits.
platform.compute: ECS on Fargate first (not EKS). Step Functions only for real multi-step orchestration (payout runs, dispute timelines). Go services ship as 6 deployables: go-identity (auth, users, currency, admin), go-commerce (catalog, inventory, orders, analytics), go-money (payments, wallet, ledger, escrow, subscriptions, creators; no rewards module, referral and purchase loyalty/cashback removed by the owner on 2026-10-03), go-live (live), go-ads (ads), go-trust (moderation).
platform.media: Media bytes live in S3 behind CloudFront; Postgres stores only metadata and keys. LiveKit carries live video.
platform.later: OpenSearch (search) and ClickHouse (seller/creator analytics) come later, fed from domain events.
platform.decisions: Python returns scores (ranking, fraud risk, moderation classification) and never makes the final financial or moderation call; Go/TS apply a deterministic policy (allow / hold / review / reject) and record it. Feed and clip ranking runs a safety/integrity filter before ranking.
platform.local: infra/local/docker-compose.yml: Postgres 17 + PostGIS, Valkey, RabbitMQ 4 with management UI on 127.0.0.1:15672 and the Prometheus endpoint on :15692 (definitions from infra/local/rabbitmq), LocalStack 4.9 (SES only), SeaweedFS (S3), LiveKit, OTel collector + Jaeger; OpenSearch and ClickHouse behind compose profiles.

messaging.topology: infra/local/rabbitmq/topology.json is the single source; pnpm backend:rabbitmq:definitions generates definitions.json (vhost zudomart, users and permissions, exchanges, queues, bindings, retry queues, DLQs). Loaded by the local broker at boot; imported into Amazon MQ through the management API on deploy.
messaging.queueComparison: SNS+SQS: serverless and cheapest per request but AWS-only (LocalStack drift locally), 15-minute max delay, no routing beyond filter policies. EventBridge: rule routing and archive/replay, ~2x SNS cost, ~10k events/s quota. Kafka/MSK: replayable log and per-partition order but the highest fixed cost and ops burden. Redis Streams: fast but weak durability, not for money. RabbitMQ (Amazon MQ): same broker locally and in AWS, topic routing per consumer, quorum queues with publisher confirms, per-queue retries/DLQs/delays without plugins, mature Go/TS/Elixir/Python clients, and launch traffic (<500 events/s, gift bursts of a few thousand/s) is far below one cluster's capacity.
messaging.why: One broker model for every stack and environment, explicit at-least-once semantics (confirms, manual acks, DLQs) that match the outbox and processed-event idempotency already in place, and no LocalStack emulation in the local loop. Replay stays with the outbox; streams or MSK are revisited if sustained throughput passes ~5k events/s or consumers need historical replay.
messaging.observability: rabbitmq_prometheus plugin locally (queue depth, consumer lag, DLQ size); Amazon MQ CloudWatch metrics and alarms in AWS (docs/architecture/observability.md 5.1).

storeMembers.why: Staff are existing Zudomart users invited by username; membership is per store, so one person can work for several sellers with the same account.

storeRoles.stack: Go catalog + Postgres; permissions copied into a short-lived store-scoped claim set cached in Redis
storeRoles.why: Owner/manager/staff presets plus custom roles; every seller endpoint checks a named permission (products.write, orders.fulfil, inventory.adjust, reports.export, team.manage, apiKeys.manage) denied by default.

locations.why: Locations cover warehouses, shops used only as pickup points, and third-party fulfilment centres; stock is per variant per location.

suppliers.why: Suppliers and purchase orders write stock movements, so they share the transaction boundary with stock levels.

stockMovements.why: Every stock change (sale, return, transfer, receipt, manual adjustment) is an immutable movement row; levels are a projection, which makes audits and reports exact.

reorder.stack: Go inventory + Postgres; demand input from python dataPipelines.forecastProductDemand
reorder.why: Reorder points are simple rules evaluated on movement; the forecast only refines suggested quantities.

storeRewards.note: Seller-funded per-store credit ledger in go-commerce (not go-money cash): redeemable only at the issuing store as a discount, never withdrawable. Added 2026-10-03.

sellerPlans.stack: Go subscriptions + Postgres; entitlements cached in Redis and enforced by the gateway and each owning service
sellerPlans.why: Free / Pro / Business. Free sellers get the full dashboard with limits (product count, locations, team seats, report history, API keys); Pro/Business raise limits and unlock exports, webhooks, multi-location and advanced analytics. Entitlements are data, not code branches.

liveProducts.why: Products are optional: a session with zero pinned products is a non-selling creator stream.

categories.why: Categories (shopping, music, gaming, talk, education) drive discovery and let creators stream without selling; listing is cache-friendly and owned next to the session it labels.

gifts.stack: Go live + wallet/ledger (coins debited via postBalancedJournalEntry), fan-out via Elixir realtime
gifts.why: Gifting is money movement at chat speed: Go gives a cheap synchronous path to the ledger with an Idempotency-Key per tap, combos are a short Redis window keyed by sender+gift+session, top gifters are a Redis sorted set rebuilt from ledger events; Phoenix PubSub fans the animation out to every viewer without touching Go.

guests.stack: Go live (state machine, max 10 publishers) + LiveKit SFU (publish grants via issueLiveKitGuestToken) + Elixir presence
guests.why: The guest seat list is authoritative state with a hard cap of 10 streamers, so it lives in Postgres behind Go with a row lock per session; LiveKit already does SFU media, Go only mints/revokes publish grants and mutes tracks through the LiveKit server API; Elixir broadcasts stage changes.

battles.stack: Go live (battle state machine + settlement through ledger journal entries, optional winner-takes-all) + LiveKit for the split-screen media + Elixir for realtime score events
battles.why: Scores come from gifts, so the authoritative score must be derived from the same idempotent gift writes; Go settles once with a balanced journal entry (normal split or winnerTakesAll moving the loser's battle earnings to the winner); Elixir pushes battleScoreChanged at sub-second latency to all viewers of both rooms.

sellerAnalytics.stack: Go analytics module (go-commerce deployable) querying an Aurora read replica now and ClickHouse (clickhouse-go v2) later; ClickHouse (added later) fed from domain events by python dataPipelines.eventIngestion; until then reads go to Aurora read replicas
sellerAnalytics.why: Day one: an Aurora read replica, because the single cluster already holds every schema and the read-only grants make cross-schema rollups possible without touching the writer. Later: ClickHouse fed from domain events, once dashboards need wide time-bucketed aggregations over views, clicks and live events at volumes where GROUP BYs on OLTP storage get slow; the query API stays the same.

reportExports.stack: Go analytics + ClickHouse + S3 signed URLs; async job on the RabbitMQ JobQueue
reportExports.why: Exports (CSV/XLSX) run off the request path, stream from ClickHouse to S3 and are gated by seller plan history limits.

sellerApiKeys.stack: TypeScript integrations (Zudojs + Prisma); keys stored as SHA-256 hashes with a visible prefix; gateway verifies via cached lookup
sellerApiKeys.why: API keys are an edge concern checked on every partner request, so they sit next to the gateway in the same runtime; scopes reuse store role permission names.

sellerWebhooks.stack: TypeScript integrations consuming domain events from its RabbitMQ queue; HMAC-SHA256 signed deliveries with retries and backoff
sellerWebhooks.why: Delivery is I/O-bound fan-out from the event bus with per-endpoint retry queues, a good fit for Node; Pro/Business only via sellerPlans entitlements.

liveStage.why: One topic per live room; Presence tracks guest seats and viewers across nodes with CRDTs.

battleScoreboard.stack: Elixir Phoenix topics fed by battle.scoreChanged domain events from the realtime RabbitMQ queue
battleScoreboard.why: A battle spans two rooms; a dedicated topic joins both audiences and coalesces score bursts to ~5 updates/second.

eventsIngestion.stack: Python (FastAPI) in apps/intelligence, internal only, HMAC-signed requests; contract in apps/intelligence/apiContract.md
eventsIngestion.why: Already built: the signed event envelope stored as Parquet and folded into online features in Redis.

feedRanking.stack: Python (FastAPI) in apps/intelligence, internal only, HMAC-signed requests; contract in apps/intelligence/apiContract.md
feedRanking.why: Already built; callers fall back to deterministic ordering when it is slow or down.

ads.stack: Python (FastAPI) in apps/intelligence, internal only, HMAC-signed requests; contract in apps/intelligence/apiContract.md
ads.why: Already built: targeting, auction, pacing and ad load; go.ads owns campaigns and billing.

recommendations.stack: Python (FastAPI) in apps/intelligence, internal only, HMAC-signed requests; contract in apps/intelligence/apiContract.md

risk.stack: Python (FastAPI) in apps/intelligence, internal only, HMAC-signed requests; contract in apps/intelligence/apiContract.md
risk.why: Already built: fraud and abuse scoring used by orders, payments, wallet and live gifts.

experiments.stack: Python (FastAPI) in apps/intelligence, internal only, HMAC-signed requests; contract in apps/intelligence/apiContract.md

audio.stack: Python (FastAPI) in apps/intelligence, internal only, HMAC-signed requests; contract in apps/intelligence/apiContract.md
audio.why: Already built: sound ownership and copyright matching for clips.
